basis: Scapuloperoneal skeletal muscle degeneration defines the disease; cardiac conduction abnormality occurred in only 1/14.
Subcutaneous fat loss with insulin resistance and dyslipidemia; hepatic steatosis is 5-29%, hepatomegaly alone insufficient; atherosclerosis is a separate disease.
Unilateral congenital formation of an additional postaxial digit.
Bile reflux affects the stomach, esophagus or pancreas; the definition does not establish liver or bile duct damage.
A bacterial infection-associated cutaneous eruption defines the condition.
Skeletal dysplasia and intellectual disability define the syndrome; both documented in 5/5. Proptosis and external ear morphology do not establish functional damage.
Abdominal obesity and metabolic syndrome; hypertension is an annotated phenotype and a major metabolic syndrome criterion.
Renal dysplasia and limb/rib malformations define the syndrome; lethal pulmonary hypoplasia occurred in all three described infants.
Malignant neoplasm arising in the liver; lymphoma is only one subtype and does not characterize the umbrella.
RPGRIP1-related retinal dystrophy causes severe visual loss; developmental delay was reported in 6/30, below 30%.
Neonatal parathyroid/calcium disorder; nephrocalcinosis and renal tubular acidosis are reported, but involvement in at least 30% is not established.
Hereditary anemia attributed to erythrocyte ATPase deficiency; no systemic metabolic or other organ disease is established.
Chronic Corynebacterium minutissimum infection of skin folds.
Hamartomatous polyp arising in colonic mucosa; local inflammation does not establish an immune-mediated disease.
Skeletal dysplasia and sensorineural hearing loss define OSMED; hearing loss and premature osteoarthritis occurred in 3/3. Proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
The disease is defined by acute lymphoblastic leukemia together with congenital absence of the iris.
Treponema pallidum infection of the brain or spinal cord; ocular damage is not established in at least 30% across the umbrella.
Benign ovarian epithelial/stromal neoplasm; reproductive tissue origin without an endocrine disorder.
Immune-mediated arterial vasculitis; neuropathy occurs in ~60-80%, renal ischemic involvement ~40-60%. GI and skin involvement omitted under the four-axis cap; hepatitis is separate.
Rhabdoid tumor located in striated muscle tissue.
Tibial peripheral nerve injury causes sensory loss and weakness; weakness does not establish a primary muscle disorder.
Obstructive mucus-filled cyst of a salivary gland; salivary glands belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Acral inflammatory dermatitis encompassing infection-related and immune-mediated eruptions; associated viral hepatitis is a separate disease.
Inherited tyrosinase-dependent melanin synthesis defect defines skin/hair depigmentation and ocular developmental abnormalities with impaired vision.
Congenital unilateral overgrowth of one or more fingers; no additional organ damage is established.
